basis: Pyogenic infection affects bone and its marrow compartment; the explicit bone-marrow-disorder parent supports the marrow axis.

decisions.haematologic: primary: osteomyelitis directly infects marrow as well as bone; the marrow axis does not require cytopenia.

basis: Forebrain and defining oral malformations; clefts 80-99%. Eye defects and endocrine dysfunction 30-79%; choanal atresia (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: the definition includes facial malformation, with oral clefts in 80-99% and characteristic dental anomalies; mouth and teeth belong to this axis.

basis: Renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia with defining intracerebral calcifications; clinical detail is limited.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intracerebral calcifications are a defining structural brain lesion of this syndrome, rather than an incidental finding.

basis: CNS, retinal and renal tumors are defining manifestations. Adrenal tumors are frequent (30-79%) in supplied HPO; ear tumors 5-29%, with hearing data from a selected series.

decisions.renal: primary: renal cell carcinoma is a characteristic tumor and part of VHL diagnostic criteria, not merely an unrelated later cancer risk.
decisions.otologic: none: endolymphatic sac tumors occur in 5-29%; the 34/35 hearing-loss series does not establish prevalence across the VHL population.

basis: Adult epithelioid sarcoma commonly originates in dermis/subcutis and extremity connective tissues, including fascia and tendons.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the usual adult/distal tumor commonly arises in dermal or subcutaneous soft tissues, which this guide assigns to skin.

basis: CNS and skeletal developmental defects define the syndrome. Respiratory insufficiency and urogenital fistula each 80-99%; variable ocular anomalies omitted at cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: short neck and delayed bone age are in the defining phenotype; short distal phalanges occur in 80-99%, supporting intrinsic skeletal malformation.

basis: FGFR1-rearranged hematopoietic neoplasm; associated lymphoblastic lymphoma is a common, defining presentation and warrants the lymphoma mechanism axis.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: lymphoblastic lymphoma is a common defining component of the FGFR1-rearranged stem-cell neoplasm, often accompanying its myeloid presentation.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease: neurologic dysfunction, hepatopathy and hearing loss each commonly >30%. Ocular disease also qualifies but is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: brain malformation or neurologic dysfunction commonly affects >30% in Zellweger-spectrum disease; the primary defect is peroxisomal metabolism.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal/visual disease is also common (>30%), but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of brain, liver and hearing involvement.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment is common (>30%) across Zellweger-spectrum peroxisome-biogenesis disorders.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with characteristic lymphopenia and neutropenia. Eczema affects roughly half of reported cases; recurrent infections alone do not establish other organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: characteristic lymphopenia and persistent or intermittent neutropenia are defining cellular defects, supporting blood-cell disease.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: chronic eczematous dermatitis affects roughly half of reported patients and represents inflammatory skin disease, rather than a transient rash.

basis: Scalp aplasia and terminal limb defects define AOS. Congenital cutaneous capillary malformation occurs in 4/6; individual cardiac and portal lesions occur in 1/6.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita in 4/6 is a structural capillary malformation, not transient mottling; capillaries belong to this axis.
